sounds.intro: Georgian has its own alphabet with 33 letters, no capitals, no genders and no articles. The Latin shown is the standard romanisation. Stress is light, so say each syllable evenly. Verbs are the hard part, but the sounds are easy once you hear the "popping" consonants.
rows: pop the sound out with a tight throat, with no puff of air
a "k" popped far back in the throat
plain, with a puff of air, like English
notes: The apostrophe in the Latin marks a popped consonant. It is the key difference between pairs such as t / t' and k / k'.
The Georgian-script line is written by rule from the Latin.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Georgian often drops the pronoun, because the verb shows who is speaking. There is no he / she difference: "is" means both.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -ebi to the noun. After a number, the noun stays singular: ori ts'igni (two book).

grammar.title: To be: var, khar, aris
text: "To be" is a real verb. Put it after the noun or adjective.

grammar.title: Makvs: have
text: Georgian says "to me there is": makvs (I have), gaqvs (you have), akvs (he or she has).

grammar.title: Present tense
text: The verb carries a prefix for who does it: v- (I), nothing (you), -s (he), v-...-t (we). Cham (to eat): vch'am, ch'am, ch'ams, vch'amt, ch'amt, ch'amen.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb often goes last, but the order is flexible. Georgian has no articles: "ts'igni" means "a book" or "the book".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "ar" before the verb: vts'er (I write), ar vts'er (I do not write). "Ar aris" means "is not".
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: A yes or no question uses the same words, with a rising voice. You can also add the little word "tu" to soften it.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand just before the verb.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Put the word before the noun: chemi (my), sheni (your), misi (his / her), chveni (our), tkveni (your, formal), mati (their). "Miqvars" means "I love" or "I like very much".

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: shen (informal): friends, family, children. tkven (formal): strangers, older people, work. Add -t to the verb for formal: khar / khart.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: The past and the future change the verb's stem and its ending. Learn each common verb as a pair: ts'avedi (I went), ts'avalo (I will go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the short form (modi). Formal: add -t (modit). To forbid, put "nu" in front.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: shemidzlia + noun form (shemidzlia tsurva). Must: unda + verb. Want: minda + verb.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Georgian uses endings, not words in front: -shi (in), -ze (on), -tan (at, near), -dan (from), -s (to).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "ufro" before the adjective for "more": ufro didi. For "the most" use "q'velaze": q'velaze didi. "Than" is -ze.
